newsitem.title: USA: Judge blocks certain California welfare cuts -ACLU.
newsitem.headline: Judge blocks certain California welfare cuts -ACLU.

text.p: A federal judge on Tuesday issued an order temporarily blocking a California law that would reduce welfare benefits to certain families, attorneys for the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) said.
The law would reduce the benefits of welfare recipients who have not lived in California for 12 consecutive months to the levels they received in the states they had left.
The ACLU sued to block the reductions, arguing that the cuts would violate the U.S. Constitution.

At a hearing in Sacramento, Judge Lawrence Karlton issued a temporary restraining order, blocking California from enacting the state law and its welfare reductions, the ACLU of Southern California said in a statement.
The restraining order will remain in effect until May 16 when a hearing on a preliminary injunction will be held, the ACLU said.
Attorneys for the state were not immediately available to comment on the decision.

Corinne Chee, a spokeswoman for the California Department of Social Services, said earlier Tuesday that the reductions were designed to prevent welfare recipients in other states from flocking to California.
"We just don't want them coming here for the higher benefit levels," Chee said.
